record.original_question: Let D = {z ∈ C^n ; h(z) < 1} be a bounded pseudoconvex complete−circular domain with Minkowski function h. Characterize the Caratheodory, the Bergman or the Kobayashi completeness of D via properties of h. [The following is known: a) If h is continuous, then D is Bergman complete. b) If n ≥ 3, continuity of h does not imply the Kobayashi completeness of D.]

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5.3 Let D = {z ∈ Cn ; h(z) < 1} be a bounded pseudoconvex complete−circular domain with Minkowski function h. Characterize the Caratheodory, the Bergman or the Kobayashi completeness of D via properties of h. [The following is known: a) If h is continuous, then D is Bergman complete. b) If n ≥ 3, continuity of h does not imply the Kobayashi completeness of D.] -P. Pflug, pflugvec@dosuni1.bitnet

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $h:\mathbb{C}^n\to[0,\infty)$ be a Minkowski function, that is, an upper semicontinuous function satisfying $h(\lambda z)=|\lambda|\,h(z)$ for all $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$, and such that the set
$$D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}^n: h(z)<1\}$$
is a bounded pseudoconvex complete circular (balanced) domain. Recall that:

- The Carathéodory pseudodistance $c_D$ on $D$ is defined by $c_D(z,w)=\sup\{\rho(f(z),f(w)): f\in\mathcal{O}(D,\mathbb{D})\}$, where $\rho$ is the Poincaré distance on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$.
- The Kobayashi pseudodistance $k_D$ is the largest pseudodistance not exceeding the Lempert function built from analytic disks in $D$.
- The Bergman pseudodistance $b_D$ is defined via the Bergman metric on $D$ (when the Bergman kernel makes this meaningful).
- $D$ is called Carathéodory (respectively Kobayashi, Bergman) complete if it is complete with respect to $c_D$ (respectively $k_D$, $b_D$).

Find a characterization, expressed purely in terms of properties of the Minkowski function $h$, of each of the following:
(i) the Carathéodory completeness of $D$;
(ii) the Bergman completeness of $D$;
(iii) the Kobayashi completeness of $D$.

(It is known that if $h$ is continuous then $D$ is Bergman complete, and that for $n\geq 3$ continuity of $h$ does not imply Kobayashi completeness of $D$.)
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that this remains an active topic: partial results exist (e.g., Bergman completeness under continuity of the Minkowski function, and a known counterexample for Kobayashi completeness in dimension ≥ 3 from continuous Minkowski functions), but no complete characterization in terms of $h$ has been published. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A counterexample for Kobayashi completeness of balanced domains
status_evidence.snippet: Constructing bounded balanced domains of holomorphy with continuous Minkowski function that are not Kobayashi-finitely-compact.
status_evidence.claim: Continuity of the Minkowski function does not imply Kobayashi completeness, showing the problem is non-trivial and a full characterization remains sought.

status_evidence.title: Hyperconvexity and Bergman completeness — Błocki and Pflug
status_evidence.snippet: Bounded pseudoconvex domains that are hyperconvex are Bergman complete.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on Bergman completeness are known but a Minkowski-function characterization is not given.

status_evidence.title: A note on the smoothness of the Minkowski function
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity of Minkowski functions of bounded pseudoconvex balanced domains.
status_evidence.claim: Research on Minkowski functions of balanced domains continues, indicating the characterization problem is still active.
